surface: The grid in its default navigation mode (headers not navigable, Tab moving between cells): Tab in from the page, arrows across cells with their headers, Tab out at both ends and back in.

steps.note: Tab from the page's control before the grid enters the grid on its first cell: its value, its column header and its place. The headers are named so a header is a fact of its own (the grid page's letters A, B and C would also match a cell reference NVDA spells A 1). VoiceOver names no row on a cell move: its behavior on a well-formed grid too. Finding (the grid's): VoiceOver with Chromium says column 1 here and counts 13 rows in this grid of five, because the overlay clones add rows of their own to Chromium's accessibility tree.

The cell to the right, which the column header names: with headers not navigable, a reader hears the header only through the cell. Finding (the grid's): NVDA with Chromium also names the previous column's header after the row (B 1, B, row 2, A, column 3 on the recording), the overlay clones' wrong header.
End moves to the last cell of the row, where Tab leaves the grid.
Tab from a row's last cell leaves the grid for the page's next control: no trap at the grid's end.
Shift+Tab from the page returns into the grid on the cell it left.
Home moves to the first cell of the row, where Shift+Tab leaves the grid.
Shift+Tab from a row's first cell leaves the grid for the page's previous control: no trap at the grid's start.
Tab from the page returns into the grid on the cell it left.
